articles.title: Monthly Observing Highlights
articles.summary: This 'Monthly Observing Highlights' for September 2025 showcases several astrophotography images of deep-sky objects like the Pelican and West Veil Nebulae, detailing their creation with specific equipment and exposure times. It also includes brief social snippets from a group observing session and a comprehensive calendar of upcoming astronomical events for late 2025, featuring planetary oppositions, meteor showers, and moon phases.

articles.title: SJAA Programs and Activities
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a comprehensive range of programs and activities for its members and the public, covering educational resources like a library, equipment support such as telescope fix-it and loaner programs, and quick start guidance for beginners. The association also hosts specialized astro-imaging groups and workshops, alongside numerous public outreach events including star parties, solar observing, and beginner astronomy forums, all aimed at fostering interest and participation in astronomy.

articles.title: Yosemite Star Party
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) successfully hosted the 'Stars Over Yosemite' star party at Glacier Point in Yosemite National Park over two nights in July. The event drew large crowds of international visitors, many new to astronomy, who enjoyed views of the Milky Way, nebulae, galaxies, and planets under the park's pristine Bortle 2 skies. Beyond the successful public outreach, volunteers also experienced wildlife encounters, explored the park's scenic beauty, and shared their passion for the cosmos.

articles.title: KIDS CORNER
articles.summary: This 'Kids Corner' segment features an engaging word search puzzle with terms related to space exploration and specific NASA missions. It also includes several 'Fun Facts' highlighting ongoing planetary missions, spacecraft achievements like OSIRIS-REX's asteroid sample return, Juno's orbit around Jupiter, and the Parker Solar Probe's close approach to the Sun.

articles.title: The View from Below the Skies
articles.summary: The article recounts a successful public star party held at Joseph D. Grant County Park on August 16, organized with the help of SJAA volunteers despite initial poor weather, attracting 182 attendees. This event marked the park's first star party since 2020, with plans for more in 2026. Additionally, the SJAA has secured a permit for member-only observing at Grant Ranch, and is currently recruiting volunteers to coordinate these future activities.

articles.title: Board Minutes
articles.summary: The board meeting minutes detail several key decisions and updates, including the approval of a new membership database and a Discord server for member interaction. Significant progress was made on the 24" Dobsonian telescope project, securing approval from the OSA General Manager for its housing at Tilton Ranch. Other discussions involved the relationship with the Parks Department for city facility use, analysis of member survey results, and clarification on the minors policy for specific positions.

articles.title: Summer Nights in The Sierras – Or – The Night I Counted Past One Hundred
articles.summary: The article features two distinct pieces: a personal narrative detailing a summer night of stargazing in the Sierras, where the author observed and counted over one hundred meteors and identified constellations. The second part reports on the retirement celebration for Teri Rogoway, a long-standing liaison from the Open Space Authority, highlighting her decade-long collaboration with the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) on various public astronomy events and outreach programs.

articles.title: SJAA By The Numbers
articles.summary: The article presents a statistical update for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) covering the period from June to September 2025. It details changes in membership, which saw a significant increase, and also tracks follower counts across various social media platforms like X, Facebook, Blue Sky, and Instagram, noting both gains and a slight dip on X.
